about: THE CARDS OF THE DANES AND THE NORTH WAY (region danes_norway: Ripa, Sliesthorp, Reric, Hleidr, Ahus, Skiringssal, Ogvaldsnes). Written 7 Oct 2026 by the region's weaver from the ports' places files (Data/places/<port>.json), the dossiers (Design/content/dossiers) and the spine (Design/content/spine.json). A draft in the game's own files, for the user to overwrite. Each card names its port with port.id in its 'when' and is listed in its site's 'do' in the places file. The words are in Data/writing/danes_norway.json under danes_norway.<port>.<card>.<slot>; a picture line for each card is there as art.<card id>. The north has no toll man: where a Frankish port has the toll, these ports have an arrival card with whoever answers for the landing (the host at Ripa, the man who speaks for the strand at Sliesthorp, the king's man under his awning at Reric, the watchman at Hleidr, the chief at Skiringssal, the old steersman at Ogvaldsnes). Silver is weighed, never counted, north of the Eider: a price in d is its weight in silver. The spine's thread flags are set only for the step they name; this file's own flags begin dn_; the places files' own flags (rr_, og_) are set where a card carries their story's ending. Small lines run through several ports: the English boys (Ripa, Skiringssal, Sliesthorp, Ogvaldsnes), the folding scale (Ripa, Reric, Ahus, Hleidr), Asulf's stick (Sliesthorp, Ogvaldsnes), Dragomir's tally (Sliesthorp, Ahus), the smith's son (Reric, Sliesthorp), the priest for Ripa (Sliesthorp, Ripa), the altar cup (Skiringssal, Ripa), the hall's last cups (Hleidr, Sliesthorp), the brew-wife's silver (Hleidr, Ahus), the skald's riddle for the weaver (Ahus, Hleidr), the comb-makers' greeting (Sliesthorp, Ahus), the painted leaves (Ripa, Skiringssal, Reric), the two women with staffs (Skiringssal, Ogvaldsnes), the drowned chief who is not drowned (Skiringssal, Ogvaldsnes). Riddles said aloud are our own plain renderings of Heidreks gatur and Vafthruthnismal; nothing is quoted from a modern translation. (?) in a note marks what is not verified; 'saga' or LATER marks what rests on a source written long after.

cards.note: Ripa, the market bank: Hroald the host (ripa.hroald) meets a Frisian boat and asks whose guest she is. An arrival card, since the north has no toll man: a stranger has no peace until a man of the place stands for him (Design/content/peoples/norse.md, later law (?); the places file's unlock ripa.guest_right). His sons pilot over the flats (unlock_pilot_ripa, story/unlocks_793.json). Hroald is invented.

cards.note: Ripa, the caster's booth, after midsummer 793: a north-way crew sold the goldsmith the gold off a book's boards, and he wraps his moulds in what is left of the leaves. The spine's threads holy_island ('also at Ripa') and book_road ('also at Ripa'); the story ripa.leaves_by_the_handful, beats 2 and 3 (sets lf_trail_north; reads bk_knows_worth). The crew kept a boy who could tally (cast.tidwine, at Ogvaldsnes until the summer of 796). Invented on the spine's frame: no source says what was taken from Lindisfarne or where it was sold (?). The leaves aboard are the flag dn_painted_leaves, which the card harbour.amber_pit.reric reads.

cards.note: Ripa, the old well: the ale-wife Tola (ripa.tola) trades news for news. A rumour that is true: pots are short on the bank, and the price is really up (price_shock; Design/content/economy/pots_glass_luxuries.md, rumour 2). She will find a hand for a boat that is a man short (hire), and wants a tenth part in a cargo, not a wage (the unlock ripa.tolas_tenth). Her sister keeps the ale-house at Sliesthorp (sliesthorp.gunnhild). Invented people; the well, oak felled 704 to 710, is the dig's.

cards.note: Sliesthorp, the brook-mouth landing: Gunulf (sliesthorp.kings_man), who speaks for the strand and from 808 is the king's man at the one gate, takes the landing gift. An arrival card. No toll is recorded here: the gift stands for one (Design/content/lore/law_tolls.md 11). Godfred came 'with his fleet and all the horsemen of his kingdom' in 804, and in 808 set Reric's merchants down here and ordered the wall with one gate (Annales regni Francorum 804, 808). That guests owed days on the wall is the game's (the work sliesthorp.work.wall_days; chain reric_808) (?). Gunulf is invented.

cards.note: Sliesthorp, Gunnhild's house, on a Christian fast day in a heathen port, before the church of about 850: a fast day. Lent is forty fast days with no meat (Capitulatio de partibus Saxoniae c. 4; the spine's calendar); the engine's 'fast' is the day, and March stands in for Lent as in the other regions' cards. The ferryman (sliesthorp.ferryman) has eels: fish is the main food here (Ibrahim ibn Yaqub, 960s, carried back). Invented people.

cards.note: Sliesthorp, the booths and the dealer's pen: who buys Frankish blades in the north. The spine's thread swords_north, hook for Sliesthorp (sets sw_buyer_known): a Dane pays double in weighed silver, the dealer in captives pays in people; after 864 the same sale is death in the west. The law: no mail out of the realm (Herstal 779), no arms to merchants (803), nothing east but by the border posts and no arms (Thionville 805), arms to Northmen on pain of death (Pitres 864): trade_rules.json laws. The dealer is cast.asulf to 815, then a successor; the Dane is invented. The story sliesthorp.double_in_silver. 'Also at Ripa': in the war years 808 to 810 the same two stand on the bank there (the story ripa.bread_for_two_hundred, beat 4), so the card comes at Ripa too in those years.

cards.note: Sliesthorp, the dealer's pen, to 806: Asulf (sliesthorp.asulf, cast.asulf) remembers every sale. The spine's thread holy_island, hook for Sliesthorp (sets lf_trail_north): the English boys went east with a Svea, because Christians cannot be sold south to the Franks. The story sliesthorp.every_lot, beat 2 and the endings 'paid_in_blades' and 'earned'. As this region has it: three boys were bought at Skiringssal in the autumn of 793 and went east at summer's end; the one who could tally (cast.tidwine) was kept by Thorleif's crew until the summer of 796 and then came the same road. The stick for Thorleif is delivered in harbour.blade_for_a_tusk.ogvaldsnes. Invented on the spine's frame.

The annals put him at Reric only at his death in 809: his asking, his sister's son Ratimir (reric.ratimir) and every word are the game's (?).
